mechanism.base: The hard overcomes the soft, the old texts say, and so metal has its way with wood. Left alone a tree grows every direction, tall and loose and full of shoots that lead nowhere. The knife gives it a shape. It takes the branch that crowds the crown, lets light in and squares the timber for a beam. Nothing in the grain asks for the edge, and all the tree becomes passes through it.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Metal, the tree grows every way at once and nothing prunes it into a shape. Height comes without a finish. Take on one rule you did not write and keep it.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Metal, the knife outruns the tree and every new shoot meets the edge. Nothing stands long enough to bear. Let one thing grow a season before anyone judges it.

catalyst.clause: the tree grows every way at once and nothing prunes it into a shape
catalyst.remedy: Take on one rule you did not write and keep it.

friction.clause: the knife outruns the tree and every new shoot meets the edge
friction.remedy: Let one thing grow a season before anyone judges it.

wide.clause: There is no shortage of Metal in you, the knife a growing tree needs to take its shape.
wide.remedy: Use it. Finish one thing to the line this month.

missing.clause: No knife near the tree, so growth goes wherever it likes and nothing gets finished.
missing.remedy: Borrow a rule, a deadline or someone above you.

spared.clause: No knife at the tree, and the tree is better for it, free to take its own shape.
spared.remedy: Keep it so. Set your own rules and keep them.

thin.clause: A small knife at a big tree, enough to shape it and never enough to cut it back.
thin.remedy: Keep it small. One rule, kept, is plenty.

excess.clause: Too much knife at a young tree, and the trunk is cut through before it can stand.
excess.remedy: Put the knife down. Rest, read, let the trunk regrow.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal makes it hard and exact, the finish growth needs. As a catalyst, the standard comes too seldom. You take charge in a crisis sooner than you earn a place, and leave most things unfinished.
function.definition_friction: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal turns it exact, a line over your growth. As a friction, the line turns inward, and you push past the task rather than keep your rank. You become the one judge you never satisfy.
function.advise_catalyst: Nothing of yours gets finished until something outside you says when. Give one deadline a month to someone else to hold. Take charge of the next small emergency at home without being asked. Send the work with one mistake left in it. Write one rule on a card and keep it for a week.
function.advise_friction: Seek Water, the Mind energy. Water feeds the tree from below, and growth returns faster than the knife takes it. Let it hold what Metal cuts. The hardest judge you answer to lives in your head. Spend one evening a week learning something nobody grades. Sleep on the next hard reply before you send it.

candidates.cta_verdict: You grow best with a line to grow against, and you finish more under someone else's rule than under your own plan.

mechanism.base: The hard prevails over the soft, and so metal comes for wood: the shears meet the hedge, the saw meets the trunk, and wild growth learns the shape it could not find alone. Unpruned, a tree grows large and fruitless. Under the edge it loses branches and gains a harvest.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: Run thin, nothing prunes you: growth in every direction and fruit in none. Your chart asks for the knife. Invite the standard, the editor, the coach with shears.
mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the cutting never stops: cut after cut until growing feels like a fault. Too much knife leaves no tree. Step back from blades that prune for pruning’s sake.

catalyst.clause: Nothing prunes you: growth in every direction and fruit in none.
catalyst.remedy: Invite the standard, the editor, the coach with shears.

friction.clause: The cutting never stops: cut after cut until growing feels like a fault.
friction.remedy: Step back from blades that prune for pruning’s sake.

wide.clause: You have plenty of Metal, the shears that turn growth into fruit.
wide.remedy: Accept the cut. Keep what survives the edit.

missing.clause: Nothing prunes the growth: reach in every direction, fruit in none.
missing.remedy: Borrow the knife: an editor, a coach, a rule.

spared.clause: Metal runs absent, and nothing cuts: growth unshaped, and unbroken.
spared.remedy: Keep it. Invite the shears on your terms.

thin.clause: Metal runs thin and unwanted: a small blade, easy to step around.

excess.clause: Weak wood breaks under strong metal: correction past what the trunk can bear, growth that stops feeling allowed.
excess.remedy: Step back from the blade. Add water.

function.definition_catalyst: Metal is your Order, and as a catalyst, it is the standard that shapes your growth: editors, coaches, reviews, rules you chose on purpose. You improve fastest under exacting eyes.
function.definition_friction: Metal is your Order, and as a friction, it is correction landing harder than you can absorb: every rule met, every critique taken, until standards stop shaping you and start shrinking you. The harshest voice you hear ends up being your own.
function.advise_catalyst: Growth loves resistance it respects. Put your work in front of one demanding person on a schedule, monthly at least. Ask for the harshest note first. Treat every review on the calendar as training, never as threat.
function.advise_friction: Standards should serve the thing growing, never the other way around. Keep the two judges whose notes make you better and mute the rest. Answer critique after a night, never in the hour. Break one harmless rule a month to remember you can.

$original.cta_verdict: Discipline reaches you as a blade, exacting people, hard standards, and every cut you accept on purpose becomes shape you get to keep.
